concepts.why: The patient has a 17-year history of migraine headaches with a visual aura of gray-white spots followed by pain behind the right eye.
The patient experiences 3 to 4 severe migraines per month lasting 3 to 7 days, with relief only from sumatriptan after trials of other medications failed.
The patient has tried multiple medications without improvement, which may indicate medication overuse headache.
The patient experiences a continuous headache on one side of the head, which is consistent with hemicrania continua.
The patient underwent an ultrasound-guided right sphenopalatine ganglion block, which failed to resolve her symptoms.
The patient experiences prolonged and frequent migraines, which may indicate status migrainosus.
The patient experiences a new and persistent headache, which is consistent with new daily persistent headache.
The patient experiences pain radiating to the right lateral jaw, ear, and down the right suboccipital region, which may indicate cervicogenic headache.
